text:
Montreal's fifth straight win came the hard way: the Canadiens went up 4-2 early in the second period, then spent most of the night watching Pittsburgh pour shots at the net before holding on 5-4 at Centre Bell. Josh Anderson, a 95th overall pick in 2012 who is still finding the net in this league, scored twice and added an assist, including a tip-in in the second period that made it 5-3.

The early scoring was frantic. Oliver Kapanen tied it on a 4 percent chance 33 seconds after Erik Karlsson's power-play goal, and Anderson followed 24 seconds later. By the time Alexandre Texier and Chris Kreider scored 27 seconds apart in the second, the Canadiens led by two. They had also created the better chances early: MTL's expected goals (a measure of shot quality) were 1.26 to 0.55 in the first period.

After that, the game tilted hard. PIT out-chanced MTL 2.13 to 0.59 in the third and finished with 70 shot attempts to 47. Our numbers say Pittsburgh deserved to win 62 percent of the time, meaning that share of simulated replays of every shot went their way. Sidney Crosby's snap shot with 3:11 left, a 53 percent look, made it 5-4, but the Penguins found no equalizer, with Jacob Fowler stopping Andrei Kuzmenko's 35 percent chance. Sergei Murashov allowed 2.0 goals more than the shots he faced should have produced.

Montreal sits on a five-game winning streak, and it also leads the season series after Pittsburgh won the October 3 meeting 6-5 in overtime. The Penguins have the better process to point to, but leaving with nothing from a game they dominated late is the harder thing to explain.
